code: library(cuplyr) library(dplyr) set.seed(1)  # Median ms per call. A sample is a batch of calls fenced with gpu_sync(); # gc() runs untimed before every batch. per_call <- function(fn, samples = 15, warmup = 3, target = 0.03) {   for (i in seq_len(warmup)) fn()   gpu_sync(); gc(verbose = FALSE)   t0 <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]; fn(); gpu_sync()   one <- max(proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t0, 1e-4)   reps <- max(1L, min(500L, as.integer(ceiling(target / one))))   t <- vapply(seq_len(samples), function(i) {     gc(verbose = FALSE)     t0 <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]     for (j in seq_len(reps)) fn()     gpu_sync()     (proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t0) / reps   }, numeric(1))   1e3 * median(t) }  # GPU memory one call leaves allocated until R's next gc(), in MB. held_mb <- function(fn) {   gc(verbose = FALSE); gc(verbose = FALSE); gpu_sync()   u0 <- gpu_memory_state()$pool_used_bytes   r <- fn(); gpu_sync()   u1 <- gpu_memory_state()$pool_used_bytes   rm(r)   (u1 - u0) / 1e6 }  pipeline <- function(d) {   d |>     filter(x > 0.1) |>     mutate(z = x * y + w) |>     group_by(g) |>     summarise(m = mean(z), n = n()) |>     arrange(desc(m)) }  n <- 1e6 df <- data.frame(g = sample.int(100L, n, TRUE), x = runif(n), y = runif(n),                  w = rnorm(n)) tb <- tibble::as_tibble(df) eg <- tbl_gpu(df, lazy = FALSE) lz <- tbl_gpu(df, lazy = TRUE)  c(eager = per_call(function() collect(pipeline(eg))),   lazy  = per_call(function() collect(pipeline(lz))),   dplyr = per_call(function() pipeline(tb))) c(eager = held_mb(function() collect(pipeline(eg))),   lazy  = held_mb(function() collect(pipeline(lz))))

what: The long tail: universal CPU fallback, factor fidelity, timestamps, base-R strings, datetime accessors, and exit-scope pins (Phase 11)
title: cuplyr (development version)
text: Phase 11 scanned dplyr 1.2.1’s test suite: string functions barely appear datetime accessors appear zero times, UNKNOWN USER FUNCTIONS inside mutate()/summarise()/filter() (closures, identity(), ifelse(), scale(), lengths(), …) hard-errored – phase leads universal fallback (L1) “long tail” surface area (L5/L6) also delivers. L1 – universal expression-level CPU fallback: mutate()/ filter()/summarise() expression shape GPU expression engine doesn’t understand now routes WHOLE verb call notified CPU fallback (original dots re-injected, .=/.keep=/.=/ .= preserved), instead hard-erroring. trigger rule precise: parser returns NULL (shape understood) -> fall back; parser THROWS (genuine user error, e.g. undefined column) -> keep throwing. single change fixes top_n()/top_frac() whole mutate_at()/mutate_all()/mutate_if()/summarise_at()/ summarise_all()/summarise_if() colwise family end--end (none tbl_gpu S3 methods – ’re plain functions build call mutate()/filter()/summarise() , L1 exactly needed) turns nine formerly-pinned cuplyr-error messages either successes dplyr’s error text. L2 – factor fidelity: three silent-wrongness bugs fixed. Mutating joins used drop factor_levels entirely (now propagated build_join_schema() keyed post-suffix column name; factor key DIFFERENT levels side routes whole join CPU fallback, since native joins compare raw codes). bind_rows() used concatenate raw factor codes across differently-leveled factor columns (now computes dplyr-matching level UNION remaps side via new gpu_remap_codes()). Factor--character bind_rows() used refuse loudly (now decodes via new gpu_decode_factor(), matching dplyr’s real “factor + character = character” contract). gpu_physical_type() documents logical (DICTIONARY32)-vs-physical (INT32 codes) type split R schema types actual GPU storage now honor consistently. L3 – timestamp literals & casts: Date/POSIXct literals first-class inside filter()/mutate() expressions (5 cuDF TIMESTAMP_* granularities), filter(d < .Date("2010-01-05")) – verbatim dplyr-test-style code – now runs natively instead hard-erroring. .Date()/.POSIXct() applied existing timestamp column lower single cudf::cast(), R’s exact default-UTC semantics (.Date.POSIXct()’s default tz really literal string "UTC", matching cuplyr’s always-UTC storage, adjustment needed). L4 – bind_rows() vctrs strictness: shared type-promotion ladder (extracted Phase 8’s set-op checker) replaces old, looser promotion table – STRING now always widest (never silently demoted), numeric+character mixes error vctrs’ message format. long-parked "4.0"--floats divergence pin retired (code path now unreachable). L5 – base-R string functions native mutate()/filter(): toupper()/tolower() (cudf::strings::to_upper()/to_lower()), nchar() (count_characters(), INT32), substr() (slice_strings(), exact R clamping semantics --range start/stop), trimws() (strip(), =), paste0()/paste() (row-wise concatenate(), sep=, R’s “genuine NA argument becomes literal string \"NA\"” rule), grepl() (contains_re()/contains() fixed=TRUE, R’s “NA element -> FALSE” rule enforced explicitly since cuDF null-propagates), sub()/gsub() (replace_re()/replace(), first-match-vs. -matches), startsWith()/endsWith() (find.hpp). Deliberately implemented (falls back CPU instead): paste()/paste0() non-STRING argument (.character() formatting replication – paste0("x", 4) "x4", "x4.0", trap), collapse=, ignore.case=/perl=/useBytes=, non-literal pattern/position argument, nchar(type != "chars"). cuDF’s regex dialect R’s TRE/PCRE – simple ASCII patterns oracle-tested. real correctness risk task found fixed: STRING-producing function nested inside comparison/arithmetic expression (e.g. toupper(x) == "ABC", nchar(x) + 1L) needs resolve_static_type() (src/expr_eval.hpp) report REAL result type every new op, libcudf’s AST evaluator throws “non-matching operand types” – fixed extending resolve_static_type() STRING-operand detection op_dispatches_to_ast() every new L5/L6 op. L6 – lubridate datetime accessors native mutate()/filter(): year()/month()/day()/hour()/minute()/second()/quarter()/ yday()/wday() (cudf::datetime::extract_datetime_component()/ extract_quarter()/day_of_year(), cast immediately native INT16 declared INT32 inside C++ handler nested usage sees real type). wday()’s cuDF WEEKDAY component ISO Mon=1..Sun=7; lubridate::wday()’s default (week_start=7, .e. Sunday) Sun=1, Mon=2, ..., Sat=7 – remapped via (w %% 7) + 1 (verified empirically, applied global lubridate.week.start option still default). MANDATORY namespace guard: since none 9 names exist base R, going native requires call’s function symbol resolve – quosure’s environment, via explicit lubridate:: qualification – EXACTLY lubridate’s function; user’s -named function, lubridate installed/attached , falls back CPU path instead (reproducing dplyr’s behavior, including “find function” error applicable) rather silently misinterpreting call. optional argument (label=, abbr=, with_year=, non-default week_start=, …) present falls back. Known, documented, accepted divergence: lubridate::second() returns fractional value sub-second-precision POSIXct input, native path truncates whole INT32 (cuDF’s SECOND component sub-second concept) – whole-second values (overwhelming majority real usage) unaffected. lubridate Suggests-soft dependency (requireNamespace()-gated); every accessor falls back naturally isn’t installed. L7 – exit: rows_insert()/rows_append()/rows_update()/ rows_patch()/rows_upsert()/rows_delete() already fallback-registered (Phase 2) – pins oracle-equality, fallback notification, in_place = TRUE rejection six explicitly. () ordinary S3 generic dplyr never gave tbl_gpu method (used hard-error “applicable method ‘’”); .tbl_gpu() now routes CPU-fallback primitive every non-native verb uses. Verified (rebuilt): top_n()/top_frac() mutate_at()/mutate_all()/mutate_if()/summarise_at()/ summarise_all()/summarise_if() colwise family work correctly post-L1 (recode() needed nothing – ’s plain vector-level function). Deliberately scope whole phase (documented, deferred omission): native rows_*() (CPU fallback already re-runs real dplyr, ’s already 100% conformant – native large effort zero additional conformance), list-columns/LIST/collect_list()/unnest() interop (nest_by()/group_nest()/nest_join()/reframe()/rowwise() stay CPU-fallback-), real DICTIONARY32 factor storage (INT32 codes + R-side levels stays design), native INT64/bit64 round-trip, FLOAT32 ingestion, floor_date()/ceiling_date()/round_date(), difftime, stringr surface, GPU roll_median(), large-window rolling aggregation (perf phase).

title: cuplyr (development version)
text: Every dplyr row-set operation now GPU-native, composed entirely existing verbs – new C++ (see ?set-ops): union(): distinct(bind_rows(x, y)) – x’s distinct rows (x’s row order), row y already present x, y’s row order. union_all(): bind_rows(x, y) – every row x, every row y, duplicates included. intersect(): distinct(semi_join(x, y, = <every column>)). setdiff(): distinct(anti_join(x, y, = <every column>)). symdiff(): setdiff(x, y) concatenated setdiff(y, x). setequal(): two anti-join cardinality checks (nrow() == 0 sides) – plain TRUE/FALSE, ignoring row order duplicates sides, matching dplyr exactly. Column compatibility: column count name set (order tolerated – y matched x name); per-column common type follows vctrs’ (strict) common-type rules – narrower package’s bind_rows() (treats STRING universally coercible) – e.g. integer column vs. character column hard error , naming offending column types, silent promotion STRING. y may plain data.frame (uploaded automatically) – unlike join verbs, generics copy= argument . Two column-type combinations real dplyr accepts fall back CPU evaluation instead erroring (cuplyr.fallback notification fires): two factor columns different level sets, factor column vs. character column (need recomputing/decoding factor codes, package’s GPU column model doesn’t support yet); Date column vs. POSIXct column (dplyr promotes POSIXct, underlying TIMESTAMP_DAYS -> TIMESTAMP_MICROSECONDS GPU cast isn’t implemented). Two factor columns identical levels fully native.

what: Joins completion: join_by(), non-equi conditions, cardinality checks, semi_join()/anti_join()/cross_join() (Phase 7)
title: cuplyr (development version)
text: Every mutating filtering join verb now runs GPU-natively full dplyr 1.2.1 surface, row order, key coalescing, suffixing, every cardinality check reproducing dplyr’s contract exactly (see ?mutating-joins, ?semi-anti-joins, ?dplyr::cross_join full per-argument documentation): join_by() DSL: equi conditions (join_by(), join_by(== b), join_by(x$== y$b)) route existing native hash-join path. Non-equi mixed conditions (>=, >, <=, <, ()/within()/overlaps() helpers pre-expand pairs ) GPU-native via cudf::mixed_join() (least one equi condition present) cudf::conditional_join() (none), including left_join()/inner_join()/full_join()/right_join()/semi_join()/ anti_join(). keep = NULL resolves per condition, per whole join (mixed join_by(c == d, >= b) drops d keeps b). na_matches = "never": NA keys never match anything (including another NA), via cudf::null_equality::UNEQUAL, every equi non-equi join type. "na" (default) additionally makes NA match NA inclusive non-equi operators (>=/<=) join_by() condition, matching dplyr’s semantics exactly. multiple=: "" (default), "", "first", "last" — resolved device-side already-sorted join maps, zero extra cost default "". unmatched=: "drop" (default) "error", raising dplyr’s exact dplyr_error_join_matches_nothing/dplyr_error_join_matches_remaining conditions (class vector, message text, offending row number verified dplyr 1.2.1 directly). relationship=: "one--one", "one--many", "many--one", "many--many", raising dplyr’s exact dplyr_error_join_relationship_* conditions violation. default (relationship = NULL) also emits dplyr’s many--many advisory warning whenever sides genuine duplicate. semi_join()/anti_join(): native via cudf::filtered_join (non-deprecated OO replacement join.hpp’s free left_semi_join/ left_anti_join). x’s group_by() grouping preserved (row filters, column-merging joins). cross_join(): native via cudf::cross_join, left-major row/column order, every common name suffixed sides. right_join() row order fix: previously emitted y-order unmatched rows; now matches dplyr’s x-matched--unmatched-y-tail contract. Implemented via device-side join-map pipeline (sanitize → stable sort → optional diagnostics → multiple= filtering → gather/coalesce) shared every mutating join type, replacing old swapped-left-join workaround. Suffix/keep edge cases: ported dplyr:::add_suffixes()/ dplyr:::join_cols() directly (already-taken suffixed name now gets second suffix, e.g. val.y.y, instead silently colliding). Falls back CPU (transparent, notified via cuplyr.fallback), deliberate design, oversight: join_by(closest(...)) / rolling joins — needs “keep extremal match per group” step package’s join kernels don’t implement; GPU route scoped Phase 12+. non-equi condition comparing STRING columns — cudf’s AST comparison evaluator string support (equi STRING joins unaffected). suffix = c("", ...) still produce genuine duplicate output column name — dplyr resolves via name-keyed column overwrite package’s fixed-column-count gather can’t express natively. nest_join() — needs list-column support (Phase 11).

Known gaps, fixed layer aren’t reached via S3 dispatch: add_tally(), top_n(), top_frac() plain (non-generic) functions dplyr 1.2 call mutate()/filter() internally constructs (n() inside mutate(), top_n_rank() inside filter()) GPU-native/CPU-eval paths verbs don’t yet understand; group_rows() group_walk() likewise non-generic work transparently since call group_data()/group_map(), now implemented.

title: cuplyr (development version)
text: Every dplyr verb now builds single AST node routes one shared execution path (push_op()/push_join() R/execute.R, lower_and_execute() R/lower.R) regardless whether table eager lazy. collapsed number eager/lazy divergences previously produced different results depending execution mode; see fixes .

title: cuplyr (development version)
text: filter(), mutate(), expressions inside summarise()’s aggregation calls now parse one shared rlang-based expression IR (R/ir.R) lowered cudf::compute_column() (src/expr_eval.hpp), replacing three separate special-cased parsers. large capability jump three verbs: filter() now understands &, |, !, xor(), arbitrarily nested combined comparisons; %% (including set containing NA empty set); .na(); (); string-column comparisons (==, !=, <, <=, >, >=) literal another string column; math columns inside predicate (+ - * / %% %/% ^, sqrt, log, abs, etc.) — surface mutate() supports. &&/|| now rejected message pointing &/|, matching dplyr 1.1+. mutate() now understands arbitrarily nested arithmetic ((x + y) * z - 1), scalar--either-side expressions (10 - x), %%/%/%, math functions (sqrt, log/log(x, base), log2, log10, exp, abs, floor, ceiling, sin, cos, tan, round()), comparisons logical operators, .na()/()/%%, NA literals (typed bare), later dots referencing earlier dots’ output columns. summarise()’s aggregation calls (e.g. sum(...), mean(...)) now accept sub-expression IR understands, just single comparison arithmetic operator — e.g. sum(carb > 3 & wt < 4), mean(sqrt(hp)), sum(carb %% 2 == 0) now work, eager lazy modes, grouped ungrouped. filter()/mutate()’s multi-expression calls now lowers exactly one fused GPU kernel (one compute_column() call), regardless many predicates/expressions deeply nested — previously operator chain separate kernel launch.

title: cuplyr (development version)
text: Fixed silent data-corruption bug lazy-mode projection-pushdown optimizer: push_down_projections() drop replaced (newly-created) column upstream projection lazy mutate() overwrote existing column didn’t read input. broke gpu_mutate_expr()’s replace--place name matching, silently appending new value end instead — rotating column values across table error warning. Found via T6 mutate() dplyr-oracle test suite; genuinely new output columns can pruned upstream requirement now. right_join() now works ; previously errored every call due internal argument-parsing mismatch. full_join() right_join() now coalesce join key columns unmatched rows instead leaving NA. example, full_join(x, y, = "id") now populates id y rows matched right side. bind_rows() now actually casts columns get type-promoted STRING (e.g. combining numeric column one table character column another). Previously promoted column kept original GPU type schema claimed STRING, causing type-mismatch failure. mutate() longer silently promotes integer arithmetic FLOAT64. +, -, *, %%, %/% now preserve INT32/INT64 every input column literal involved integer logical (matching R/dplyr, e.g. TRUE + TRUE 2L). INT32 results leave R’s integer range NA warning, R (F42; wrapped around F42). / ^ continue always promote FLOAT64 (matching R: 1L / 2L 2L ^ 2L doubles). arrange(..., .by_group = TRUE) now sorts prepended group columns ascending order match dplyr::arrange.grouped_df(), even user’s expression wraps group column desc() (e.g. arrange(desc(g), x, .by_group = TRUE) now sorts g ascending, x per user’s spec). filter(TRUE) now true -op: returns .data unchanged without GPU work, instead round-tripping filter kernel. Lazy summarise() sd()/var() longer errors. Lazily evaluated aggregations now translate cudf function names (std/variance) eager path always used. summarise() now accepts namespaced aggregation calls, e.g. dplyr::n() stats::sd(mpg), eager lazy modes. summarise(n = n()) now always returns integer (INT32) column, matching dplyr. Previously, ungrouped n() silently returned double due schema/GPU-column type mismatch. summarise() unnamed aggregation expression (e.g. summarise(mean(mpg))) now auto-names output column expression text warns, matching mutate()’s existing behavior unnamed expressions. regressed silently neither either mode. Eager select() factor column now round-trips factor collect(). Previously eager path dropped factor level metadata, collect() returned integer codes instead factor labels.

title: cuplyr (development version)
text: Added cuplyr.fallback option control whether filter()’s summarise()’s CPU-evaluation fallback paths notify caller. One "silent" (default), "warn", "error".

title: cuplyr 0.1.1
text: collect() now correctly restores factor columns original levels. Previously, factor columns returned integer codes instead factors (#3). names<-() now validates replacement value assignment. errors new names wrong length, contain NA values, empty strings, character (#4).

title: cuplyr 0.1.1
text: Fixed CCCL (CUDA Core Compute Libraries) header detection RAPIDS 25.12+ pixi/conda environments headers located rapids/ subdirectory. configure script now automatically detects <cuda/stream_ref> related headers. Reordered include paths CUDF/RMM headers take precedence system CUDA headers, ensuring consistent CCCL versions.

title: cuplyr 0.1.1
text: Added pkgdown documentation site vignettes getting started, complex analysis workflows, query optimization.

title: cuplyr 0.1.0
text: tbl_gpu() gains lazy argument enable deferred execution. Operations build AST (Abstract Syntax Tree) optimized executed collect() compute() called. Set globally options(cuplyr.exec_mode = "lazy") CUPLYR_EXEC_MODE=lazy environment variable. Added AST optimizer applies multiple optimization passes execution: Projection pruning: push column selection close data sources Mutate fusion: combine consecutive mutate operations Dead column pruning: remove unused intermediate columns Filter pushdown: move filters earlier pipeline, including across joins Filter reordering: execute cheaper filters first Filter fusion: combine multiple filters single GPU kernel compute() executes pending lazy operations keeps result GPU. collapse() inserts optimization barrier without executing. as_lazy() as_eager() switch execution modes mid-pipeline. is_lazy() has_pending_ops() check current execution state. show_query() displays pending operation tree debugging (since F05 method dplyr’s generic returns input invisibly).

title: cuplyr 0.1.0
text: Added inner_join(), left_join(), right_join(), full_join() combining GPU tables (#2). Joins support automatic key detection (natural join), named vectors different key names, suffix column name conflicts, keep retaining join keys, copy auto-transfer data frames GPU.

title: cuplyr 0.1.0
text: Added bind_rows() vertically combining GPU tables automatic schema unification type promotion. Added bind_cols() horizontally combining GPU tables .name_repair duplicate column handling. bind functions automatically materialize lazy tables binding.

title: cuplyr 0.0.1
text: Initial release cuplyr, GPU-accelerated dplyr backend using NVIDIA’s libcudf library.

title: cuplyr 0.0.1
text: tbl_gpu() transfers R data frames GPU memory, returning tbl_gpu object works dplyr verbs. collect() transfers GPU data back R tibble. as_tbl_gpu() coerces data frames GPU tables. is_tbl_gpu() tests object GPU table.

title: cuplyr 0.0.1
text: filter() supports scalar comparisons (x > 5, x == "") column--column comparisons (x > y). Supports boolean vectors filter masks. select() supports column selection name, position, tidyselect helpers. mutate() supports arithmetic operations (+, -, *, /, ^) scalars columns. Supports left-associative chains (e.g., + b + c). arrange() sorts one columns desc() support descending order. Supports .by_group = TRUE grouped tables. group_by() sets grouping metadata subsequent aggregation. ungroup() removes grouping. summarise() computes grouped aggregations support sum(), mean(), min(), max(), n(), sd(), var(). Supports expressions inside aggregation functions (e.g., sum(x > 0)).

title: cuplyr 0.0.1
text: Supported R types: numeric (FLOAT64), integer (INT32), character (STRING), logical (BOOL8), Date (TIMESTAMP_DAYS), POSIXct (TIMESTAMP_MICROSECONDS). factor columns converted INT32 codes. integer64 columns converted FLOAT64 warning precision loss values exceeding 2^53.

title: cuplyr 0.0.1
text: gpu_memory_usage() estimates GPU memory footprint tbl_gpu object. gpu_memory_state() returns current GPU memory usage (total, free, used). gpu_gc() forces garbage collection free GPU memory unreferenced tables. gpu_object_info() returns detailed information GPU table. verify_gpu_data() confirms data resides GPU, R memory. gpu_size_comparison() compares R object size vs GPU data size.

title: cuplyr 0.0.1
text: has_gpu() checks compatible GPU available. gpu_details() returns GPU device information (name, compute capability, memory).
